anatomy_key_learnings.finding: SMPL-X and other advanced systems encode physically realizable actuator configurations with strict mechanical limits and inverse kinematics for collision avoidance. Idealized stick figures use unconstrained axis-angle rotations, allowing impossible positions and self-intersections.
anatomy_key_learnings.application_to_poseart: PoseArt currently uses basic forward kinematics (FK) with a single rotation axis per joint in `buildPose`. Adding joint angle clamping based on human biomechanical limits will prevent impossible poses.

anatomy_key_learnings.finding: Natural, flattering poses usually follow an 80/20 weight distribution where 80% of weight is on the back foot and 20% on the front, creating a natural hip pop and spine curve.
anatomy_key_learnings.application_to_poseart: Implementing an auto-balance feature or preset poses that automatically adjust spine tilt and hip rotation (using the existing `hipsTiltDeg`) when leg angles differ significantly.

anatomy_key_learnings.finding: Locked joints (straight limbs) create visual tension and stiffness. A slight bend in knees, elbows, and wrists is required for a natural appearance.
anatomy_key_learnings.application_to_poseart: Introduce a minimum angle or 'softness' offset for knee and elbow joints to prevent perfectly straight 0-degree angles in default poses.

anatomy_key_learnings.finding: Subjects should almost always be angled 30-45 degrees away from the lens to create a diagonal line and shrink body space in the frame.
anatomy_key_learnings.application_to_poseart: Set the default camera yaw (`state.camYaw`) to 30-45 degrees rather than straight on (0 degrees) for better initial presentation.

skeleton_improvement_techniques.description: Never allow elbows or knees to be perfectly straight (0 degrees). Add a slight default bend (e.g., 5-10 degrees) to create visual softness.
skeleton_improvement_techniques.implementation_hint: In `buildPose`, enforce a minimum bend angle for `leftElbow`, `rightElbow`, `leftKnee`, and `rightKnee` if the user sets them close to 0.

skeleton_improvement_techniques.description: Restrict joint rotations to natural human limits to prevent broken-looking poses.
skeleton_improvement_techniques.implementation_hint: Add a configuration object with min/max angles for each joint, and clamp the values in `buildPose` before applying `rotX`, `rotY`, or `rotZ`.

skeleton_improvement_techniques.description: Instead of drawing straight lines between joints, render tapered polygons to represent muscle mass (thicker at the shoulder/hip, thinner at elbow/knee).
skeleton_improvement_techniques.implementation_hint: Update the 2D canvas drawing function (`renderFrame`) to use `ctx.beginPath()` with offset points perpendicular to the bone direction, rather than simple `ctx.moveTo()`/`ctx.lineTo()` strokes.

skeleton_improvement_techniques.description: The spine is not a single rigid stick. A natural pose requires independent rotation for the lower back (lumbar) and upper back (thoracic) to create the S-curve.
skeleton_improvement_techniques.implementation_hint: The current skeleton only has `spine` and `neck`. You need to add a `midSpine` joint to `T_POSE` and `BONES`, and update `buildPose` to distribute the `spineDeg` rotation across two joints.

competitor_findings.what_they_do_better: Offers full 3D models with both Forward Kinematics (FK) and Inverse Kinematics (IK), allowing users to drag hands/feet directly. They also have thousands of scene presets.
competitor_findings.steal_this: IK-like interaction or visual hints. Even without true IK, allow users to select an end-effector (like a hand) and use a slider to bend the elbow to reach a target.
competitor_findings.implementation_hint: Implement a simple heuristic IK solver or add UI controls that adjust multiple joints simultaneously (e.g., a 'reach' slider).

competitor_findings.what_they_do_better: Provides sensitive joint control with highlights on movable parts and a mirroring function for symmetrical poses.
competitor_findings.implementation_hint: Add a UI button that copies joint angles from left side (e.g., `leftShoulder`, `leftElbow`) to right side (`rightShoulder`, `rightElbow`) or vice versa.

competitor_findings.what_they_do_better: Separates controls (bend, tilt, rotate) and explicitly features 'Biological constraints' to prevent unnatural posing, solving the main complaint against PoseMyArt.
competitor_findings.implementation_hint: Add a checkbox in the UI that enables/disables the joint angle clamping mentioned in the anatomy section.

competitor_findings.what_they_do_better: Allows locking specific joints to act as a fulcrum, and uses a Pose Scanner to extract poses from 2D images.
competitor_findings.implementation_hint: Add a state array `lockedJoints`. When adjusting a parent joint, if a child is locked, apply counter-rotation to the child to keep its global position fixed.

anatomical_fixes: Bend one knee significantly more than the other
Ensure hips are positioned directly over the knee or heel
Add ankle rotation to flatten feet against the floor

common_problems: Body looks stiff like a board
anatomical_fixes: Use the new globalTilt/globalTwist to angle the body
Ensure the shoulder touching the ground is pushed up slightly (closer to neck)
Tilt hips (hipsTiltDeg) to match the weight-bearing leg

common_problems: Hips don't align with the seat
anatomical_fixes: Use hip abduction (hipAbductL/R) to spread legs naturally
Ensure 90-degree bend at hips and knees

top_5_skeleton_improvements.why: Prevents the 'broken doll' effect and forces users into natural pose boundaries, similar to SetPose's biological constraints.
top_5_skeleton_improvements.implementation: Add an object defining min/max angles for each joint property (e.g., `leftElbow: [0, 150]`) and apply `Math.max(min, Math.min(max, angle))` in `buildPose`.

top_5_skeleton_improvements.why: Significantly speeds up workflow for symmetrical poses, a key feature praised in Easy Pose.
top_5_skeleton_improvements.implementation: Add a function that copies values like `jointAngles.leftArm` to `jointAngles.rightArm`.

top_5_skeleton_improvements.why: Transforms the crude stick figure into a more elegant mannequin style without needing full 3D models.
top_5_skeleton_improvements.implementation: In the canvas `renderFrame` method, draw tapered polygons instead of lines by calculating perpendicular normals to the bone vector and drawing a shape that is wider at the proximal joint and narrower at the distal joint.

top_5_skeleton_improvements.why: Locked knees and straight arms make figures look rigid and amateurish.
top_5_skeleton_improvements.implementation: Change the default angles for elbows and knees from 0 to something like 5 or 10 degrees, and set the default camera yaw to 30-45 degrees.

top_5_skeleton_improvements.why: A single spine joint cannot represent the natural S-curve of the human back, which is crucial for elegant photography posing.
top_5_skeleton_improvements.implementation: Modify `T_POSE` to include a `midSpine` joint halfway between `hips` and `spine` (thoracic), update `BONES` to connect them, and distribute spinal rotation across both in `buildPose`.
